correctness.rationale: The exact conditional squared-error identity follows from summing four weighted coordinate transitions, with coefficient \(2\alpha(1-\alpha)/S\) and smallest singular value \(1-\rho\). Jensen gives all orders \(0<p\le2\); Markov plus summability gives almost-sure convergence. The two rare off-diagonal transitions jointly give a power-mean lower bound and an explicitly diagonalizable symmetric 2x2 map W, whose least singular value is \(\alpha/\rho-(1-\alpha)\) on the stated domain. This yields uniform conditional order-p growth by L_p, iterates for every x0 and k by independence, and diverges as \(\rho\downarrow0\) for fixed \(p>2\). Verified exact-rational identities and exhaustive finite paths supplement, not replace, the proof. All quantifier and near-identity boundaries were checked.

value.rationale: The motivating 2018 double-stochastic linear solver advertises global geometric mean-square convergence at alpha=1/n. The theorem establishes the nontrivial missing robustness boundary: near-identity SPD matrices can nevertheless exhibit arbitrarily strong geometric growth of any requested \(p>2\) error moment, even from every starting direction, while almost-sure convergence survives. This sharp order-two distinction gives a precise reason not to infer high-confidence/tail error guarantees from mean-square rates, and motivates entrywise safeguards. It is a structural example for a real solver, not an arbitrary parameter slice. It makes no downstream optimality or stationary-heavy-tail claim.
